'''Sima Marković''' (8 November 1888 – 19 April 1939) was a Serbian mathematician, communist and socialist politician and philosopher, known as one of the founders and first leaders of the [[Communist Party of Yugoslavia]].

== Biography ==
Marković was a doctor of mathematical sciences and a university professor. He has written many works in mathematics, philosophy, physics and politics.<ref name="Elietz">{{Cite web|url=http://www.mladina.si/43878/razkrita-titova-moskovska-skrivnost/|title=Razkrita Titova moskovska skrivnost|date=16 July 2008|accessdate=15 March 2021|website=Mladina.si|language=Slovenian|archive-date=21 August 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240821200220/https://www.mladina.si/43878/razkrita-titova-moskovska-skrivnost/|url-status=live}}</ref>

He was an early activist and member of the [[Serbian Social Democratic Party (Kingdom of Serbia)|Serbian Social Democratic Party]] in the Kingdom of Serbia, and since the unification of the Yugoslav communists in 1919 a member of the Communist Party of Yugoslavia.<ref name="automatski generisano2">{{Cite web|url=https://www.novosti.rs/dodatni_sadrzaj/clanci.119.html:278118-Drakonski-sud-partije|title=Drakonski sud partije|website=www.novosti.rs|access-date=2020-04-20|archive-date=2020-11-30|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201130120528/https://www.novosti.rs/dodatni_sadrzaj/clanci.119.html:278118-Drakonski-sud-partije|url-status=live}}</ref>

Sima Marković advocated the preservation and peaceful reform of [[Yugoslavia]] into the republic, as opposed to the then position of the [[Comintern]]. He was killed in [[Stalinist purges]] in 1939 along with many other leading Yugoslav communists. He was rehabilitated on 10 June 1958 by a decision of the Supreme Court of the Soviet Union.<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=UWALiF59JU4C&q=Sima+Markovi%C4%87&pg=PA116|title=Biographical Dictionary of the Comintern|first=Milorad M.|last=Drachkovitch|date=April 20, 1986|publisher=Hoover Press|isbn=9780817984038|via=Google Books}}</ref>
